intentional: THE DEITY ATLAS'S UNIFORM 2/4/2/1 NODE GRAPH IS A WRITTEN TEMPLATE, NOT AN ACCIDENT. The overlap analysis calls this its 'largest and best-evidenced finding' — all ten deity trees identical at depth 0:2, depth 1:4, depth 2:2, depth 3:1, zero variation. I reproduced the histogram exactly. But DESIGN-GUIDE-CLAIMS.md §PART 2 prescribes it verbatim: 'Cleanest shape has 9 talents (2 entries + 4 tier-2 riders + 2 tier-3 synthesis + 1 capstone),' and §Prerequisite patterns specifies the edges one by one — entries `[C1] 2+; [C2] 2+`; tier-2 prereqs one entry; tier-3 prereqs `[A] or [B]`; capstone prereqs one tier-3. That is the 2/4/2/1 DAG, edge for edge. The same is true of the price list the analysis flags: guide says '1 Investiture = entry-level routine, 2 = tier-2/synthesis, 3 + once-per-scene = capstone' and the trees comply. This is ten trees passing a conformance test, reported as sameness. The contrast proves the intent is deliberate: the LEYLINE guide's Principle 8 says 'Each tree meets its own needs. Do NOT impose a uniform node count or structure across all 15 trees' — and the five leyline trees have five different shapes (Black runs to depth 5, Blue stops at 4, White opens with 5 entries not 4). Two atlases, two opposite instructions, both followed.

THE HEROIC ATLAS REPRODUCES THE OFFICIAL COSMERE HEROIC ACTION-TYPE DISTRIBUTION TO WITHIN ONE PERCENTAGE POINT ON ALL SEVEN ROWS. The guide prints the official benchmark it was derived from ('Based on analysis of 374 official talents across 6 Heroic paths and 9 Radiant paths'): Passive 34% / Special 30% / Action 14% / 2 Actions 8% / Free 7% / Reaction 5% / 3 Actions 2%. Measured across all 150 heroic talents: Passive 34% / Special 29% / Action 14% / 2 Actions 8% / Free 7% / Reaction 5% / 3 Actions 3%. Seven for seven. No analysis in this review ran that comparison, and it is the single strongest evidence in the corpus that a whole atlas was built to spec and hit it.

BOTH DEFECTS THE LEYLINE GUIDE NAMED IN ITS OWN TEXT HAVE BEEN FIXED, MEASURABLY. The guide states: 'The current leyline trees have 0% Specials and 14% 3-Action costs — both need fixing. Specials are the most important gap.' Today: leyline 3-Action talents = 0 of 125 (target 0%, exact), and Specials = 27 of 125 (22%), with Red 32%, Green 28%, White 24% and Blue 20% all inside or adjacent to the 25-30% target. The revision pass the guide demanded ran and landed on four of five trees. Leyline also hits the 2-Action target (8%) exactly. Only Black misses badly (4% Special, 60% Passive against a 35% ceiling) — that one is a real violation of Revision Principle 4 and I concede it below.

EVERY DEITY TREE HAS EXACTLY ONE 3-ACTION TALENT AND IT IS ITS CAPSTONE — 10 of 90, one per tree, zero exceptions. The deity guide's most emphatic structural rule is '3 Actions: Capstones only — one per tree, max' and §PART 8 lists '3-Action talents below the capstone' as a named pitfall. Perfect compliance across ten trees. The brief flags this in passing ('which is what the deity guide prescribes') and then never credits it.

DEITY TALENTS OUT-POWERING LEYLINE TALENTS IS THE STATED TARGET, NOT A BUG. Leyline Revision Principle 9, verbatim: 'Leyline mages are mortal. Comparable to Heroic path characters, not Radiants… Strong and versatile, but human-scale. Radiant-equivalent power lives in the Deity Domain trees.' Deity Principle 9: 'Deity power is Radiant-tier… Don't undersell the capstones.' So the confirmed 5.2x per-talent damage-formula density gap (deity 33.3% vs leyline 6.4%), deity's liberal Vital/Spirit use, and deity's front-loaded depth-0 damage are all the design executing a written instruction. The primer sets the correct failure test and it is a different one: '9 deity talents outclassing 25 leyline talents in TOTAL would be' a bug. Nobody in this review ran the total-per-tree comparison; every deity-beats-leyline number offered is per-talent, which is the axis the design deliberately tilted.

LEYLINE↔HEROIC GATE-TIMING PARITY IS ALREADY ACHIEVED, AND IS THE ANSWER TO DESIGNER QUESTION 2. Counting every talent behind a rank-3 prerequisite (all skills, not just colours) from all-talents.json: heroic trees carry Warrior 6, Scholar 6, Hunter 6, Envoy 6, Agent 7, Leader 5 (mean 6.0); leyline trees carry White 5, Black 5, Red 6, Blue 8, Green 8 (mean 6.4). That is near-perfect pacing symmetry between the two atlases the designer wants at parity. Six analyses in this review reported the opposite because they believed the tooling was mis-dating heroic talents — see measurementArtefacts #1.

BLUE AND WHITE DEALING NO DAMAGE IS THE DESIGN, AND THE PLAYER-FACING TEXT SAYS SO IN A SENTENCE. INTENT-leyline-Blue.md: 'They rarely meet force with force. A Blue mage prefers to know, to prepare, and to redirect.' INTENT-leyline-White.md: 'They draw their power from unity rather than self. A White mage rarely wins alone.' Both path descriptions are damage-free by construction and promise exactly what the trees deliver. The designer's own framing confirms it ('That was originally part of the design'). The live question is not whether the absence was intended — it plainly was — but whether the replacement is felt.

THE 50%-UPTIME INVESTITURE THROTTLE IS A COMPUTED CONSEQUENCE OF A RULE THE DESIGNER WROTE, NOT AN EMERGENT FAULT. Draw Mana returns Investiture equal to Tier; at Tier 1 that is 1 Action for 1 Investiture, so a 1-Investiture-per-Action kit sustains at 50%. The primer derives this itself and names the intended lever: 'Bonus-regen talents are the lever that breaks this; count them.' The nine Investiture producers are therefore the designed escape hatch, and their distribution (Black 2, Red 1, one free Passive each in Chaos/Knowledge/Life/Death/Sovereignty) is the design choosing which trees get to break the throttle. Note the special case that inverts the 'White has an empty turn' complaint: White is the only colour whose refuel Action is itself an effect (the Key heals every ally in range for Tier), and Beacon of Stability is a Special that rides that same Draw Mana to strip a condition. A White player's Draw Mana turn produces a party heal plus a condition removal — the one tree in the game with no dead refuel round.

WHITE BEING ACTION-LIGHT IS REVISION PRINCIPLE 1 CARRIED TO ITS CONCLUSION. The guide's first revision principle is 'Specials first. When revising a talent that says "costs 1 Action to do X when Y happens," ask whether it could be a Special instead,' and the primer reinforces it: 'Special is the workhorse action type in official Cosmere design… A Special is worth materially more than an Action of the same effect size,' plus 'A talent that reproduces a standard action is worth roughly zero.' White's 1-Action/2-Action count of 2 in 25 is that instruction over-obeyed, not ignored. Same for the count of 7 Reactions: the guide never caps Reaction breadth, and White's seven have five distinct trigger classes (ally takes damage / ally is influenced / ally would fail a test / ally rolls a Complication / enemy targets an ally), so the slot is rarely idle, which is what a reactive bodyguard should feel like.

THE THREE 'SEALED LOOP' RESOURCES THE CENSUS FLAGS ARE DEITY PRINCIPLE 5 WORKING. 'Homebrew resources should be the spine of the tree, not a side mechanic. If a deity introduces a resource token… it should be generated by an entry and spent by most of the rest of the tree. Resources that only one or two talents interact with are usually a sign the tree's economy hasn't been thought through.' Omen 3/2, Quarry 1/9, Harvested Remain 5/3, Ordained Ground 7/4, Snare 5/4, Edict 3/1 are self-contained by instruction. A sealed loop is the pass condition here, not the failure.
measurementArtefacts: THE '42 MIS-DATED TALENTS' BUG DOES NOT EXIST IN THE DATA AS SHIPPED TODAY — AND IT IS THE MOST-CITED FINDING IN THE WHOLE REVIEW. Six analyses call it the highest-value repo fix ('THE MEASUREMENT FIX, and it is the most valuable thing in the analysis'). I tested it directly: of 365 talents, 75 carry an 'X 3+' prerequisite, and the number whose earliestLevel is below 6 is ZERO. Every non-colour gate is already honoured. The `rankGate` field is populated with the non-colour skill name (Devastating Blow `rankGate=Athletics 3+`, Wit's End `Intimidation 3+`, Foresight `Discipline 3+`, Turning Point `Deduction 3+`). The dossier .md files print it too: heroic-Warrior.md reads 'Devastating Blow … depth: 1 | earliest L6'. Either the data was regenerated after those analyses ran, or the analysts generalised from the damage-census.js `earliestL` COLUMN (a per-tree aggregate over damage-source talents only, which is where heroic/Warrior's misleading '2' lives) to the per-talent field. Before anyone spends a session fixing derive-dossiers.js, re-run my check. Note carefully: the CONCLUSIONS drawn from the phantom bug are right — heroic really is back-loaded to L6 and pacing really is symmetric — they were just reached through a defect that is not there.

THE BRIEF'S OWN 'STRUCTURAL FACT YOU MUST ACCOUNT FOR, NOT REDISCOVER' IS THE ERROR. The brief states: 'heroic paths carry NO leyline-colour rank gate, so their whole tree is reachable by ~L4-L5.' The clause is true and the conclusion does not follow — heroic paths carry 36 NON-colour rank-3 gates instead, 5 to 7 per tree, and the data dates every one of them L6. Every analysis that took this sentence at face value produced a leyline-is-uniquely-back-loaded finding, then rediscovered the L6 wall and blamed the calculator rather than the brief.

'FOUR OF FIVE DEITY TOLL BOOTHS ARE WHITE' IS A SEARCH-SCOPE ARTEFACT. deity-gate-audit.js counted only skill-TEST fields and damage-die sizing. Grepping the authored overlays for how a colour is actually cashed in — `skills.<colour>.rank` in any formula, plus the `color`/`rangeColor` targeting field — gives: Order/White 4 rank-refs + 2 colour-refs; Civilization/White 5 rank-refs (the Combat Construct's HP AND its 'Construct Slam' attack dice are `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2)` — White is that tree's damage die, and the census called it a toll); Knowledge/Green 5 colour-refs (Green sizes Attunement Range); Sovereignty/White 1 rank-ref (`(@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2)` sizes Sovereign's Favor's temp HP). Exactly ONE pure toll booth survives in the entire deity atlas: Fate/White, zero refs of either kind. The headline pattern 'White is gated by four deity trees and mechanically rewarded by none of them' is 1-for-4 wrong.

THE 15-AXIS RUBRIC HAS NO CELL FOR SOVEREIGNTY'S ENTIRE FUNCTION, AND SYSTEMATICALLY PENALISES DAMAGE DELIVERED THROUGH AN ALLY. The axis set has damage_direct and damage_scaling, which score self-delivered damage, and buff, which is a catch-all. deity/Knowledge converts a mark into a party-wide damage multiplier and scores damage_direct 5 / damage_scaling 5 because it also swings the sword; deity/Sovereignty converts an Action into a damage multiplier on an ally and scores damage_direct 0 / buff 3. Same function, opposite scores. Sovereignty is the purest through-ally amplifier in the game and is therefore the axis set's worst-case input. Its 'nine axes at zero, lowest axis sum in the game (13)' headline compounds this with a size artefact: all ten 9-talent deity trees score 3-9 zeros (mean 5.8) against all five 25-talent leyline trees at 2-3. Comparing Sovereignty's 9 to Blue's 3 measures talent count.

THE COSINE-SIMILARITY MATRIX IS NOT AN ARBITER AND ITS OWN AUTHORS PROVED IT. Black↔Red at 0.920 is the top pair of 210 while Black is 5 vital / 0 energy and Red 6 energy / 0 vital — opposite damage types, which the vector cannot see. The `deal_damage` classifier misses 33 of 43 formula-carrying talents (77% blind). And the Blue↔Scholar re-check showed rank moving from 10 → 20 → 25 → ~122 depending on which dimensions you pick, i.e. the metric is dominated by dimension selection rather than by the talents. Meanwhile the guide's Principle 7 ('Talents must not bleed across color lines') is a boundary condition about EFFECT TYPE — heal depth, Injury removal, isolate vs cluster — which the function vector does not encode at all. A high cosine between two trees that obey Principle 7 is measuring shared sentence shape.

'ADVANTAGE IS OVER-PRODUCED, 45 TALENTS' IS ~2.5x OVER-COUNTED ON THE MEASURE THAT MATTERS. The true producer count is 36, and only about 15 of those can land on an attack roll. The other ~21 sit on non-colliding skills — Cognitive (Blue Key, Sleuth's Instincts), Perception and tracking (Primal Awareness, Predator's Instinct), Deception (Predatory Insight), Intimidation/Insight/Agility (three Warrior stances that are mutually exclusive modes anyway), stealth (Shadowing, Shadow Step), social (both Well Dressed), Erudition (Strategize), Deduction (Close the Case, Turning Point). Since a PC holds one leyline plus one heroic path or one deity tree, the acute redundancy is three specific pairings (Green+Hunter, inside Order, inside Power), not an ecosystem-wide glut. And where a free grant exists, a competent player simply never buys the paid one — the cost is a talent slot, not a wasted resource.

CROSS-TREE 'STRICT DOMINATION' COMPARES CHOICES NO PLAYER MAKES. Claims of the form 'Sovereignty's Exalt is dominated by Knowledge's The Pack' or 'Death's Risen Servant is dominated by Civilization's Forge Construct' describe a spreadsheet adjacency, not a decision. A player picks a deity — which god their character serves — and gets nine talents; the comparisons they actually make are inside that tree. This does not exempt the deity-parity question the designer asked, which is legitimately cross-tree; it means domination language should be reserved for in-tree pairs. Two of the eight claimed dominations already collapsed on reading (Risen Servant sustains up to TIER servants against Forge Construct's one; Kneel's advantage clause is a free standing rider fed by the Black Key that every Power character carries).

150 OF 365 TALENTS WERE JUDGED AGAINST STANDARDS THAT DO NOT COVER THEM. DESIGN-GUIDE-CLAIMS.md contains exactly two standards, LEYLINE and DEITY. There is no heroic design guide. Every heroic criticism in this review — flat damage formulas, shared stock, Action-type mix, [Tier][Die] absence — measures the heroic atlas against leyline/deity conventions it was never written to. What it WAS written to is the official Cosmere heroic benchmark, and it hits that 7 rows out of 7 (intentional #2).

'HEROIC DAMAGE DOESN'T SCALE' MEASURES ONE CHANNEL OF THREE. The heroic atlas contains only five damage formulas in 150 talents; two (Devastating Blow, Wit's End) carry `max(@tier - 2, 0)` terms that are dead until Tier 3 / level 11, and two are flat (4d4, 2d4). But heroic talents scale on SKILL RANKS, which is the atlas's actual growth channel — Scholar's three heal formulas are literally `@skills.med.rank` and `@skills.lor.rank`, and Hunter's Afflicted is rank-scaled. And every heroic damage talent is a rider on a weapon attack that grows with equipment. Excluding weapon dice 'on both sides' is not symmetric: leyline damage talents are self-contained, heroic ones are not, so the exclusion subtracts real output from one side of every comparison. Weapons are outside the scope fence, so the honest statement is that the heroic-vs-leyline damage ratio cannot be settled inside the 365 — what would settle it is the weapon damage table.

THE BLUE PLOT-DIE FINDING RESTS ON A LINE THE DESIGN GUIDE ITSELF DEPRECATES. 'Plot Die manipulation is Blue's capstone identity' lives in LEYLINE GUIDE §PART 4: COLOR IDENTITIES, whose first line, at DESIGN-GUIDE-CLAIMS.md:77, reads: '> **Note:** Attunement/Physical/Cognitive have been replaced by Specialties. The descriptions below are reference, not law.' The section is self-labelled non-binding, and the same section hands 'Plot Die integration' to White as well — two colours, one key mechanic, which is the tell that the section is stale. The BINDING intent source, INTENT-leyline-Blue.md, promises Foresight, Calculation and Illusion and never mentions the plot die; Blue implements all three specialties (8 Illusion talents, and Blue is the only tree in 365 that CREATES illusions). Compare the DEITY guide's Part 4, which carries no such disclaimer — which is precisely why the Sovereignty/Decree and Power/Bounty drifts are real and the Blue/plot-die drift is not. Six analyses call the Blue plot-die gap 'the cheapest high-value fix on the list'; it is a fix to a deprecated sentence.

MOMENTUM'S EDGE IS PROBABLY A ONE-TOKEN OVERLAY TYPO PRESENTED AS A RED IDENTITY CRISIS. The card reads 'bonus impact damage equal to your Speed' with no 'ft' and no 'rate'. Every other attribute-reading rider in the corpus means the modifier (Withering Ray '+ Presence', Withering Touch '+ WIL', Snare '+ Awareness'), and Speed is a tested skill in this system (Destruction's Concussive Yield 'tests Speed vs. your Red'; Fate's Inevitable Snare 'tests Speed vs. your Green'). The authored handler is `"bonusFormula": "@movement.walk.rate"` — the movement-rate reading — with `damage.formula: null`, so nothing rolls it through the damage pipeline. The likely truth is a wrong token in one authored rule, not a talent that needs redesigning.
trueButInvisible: [LEAST FELT] The deity atlas's uniform 2/4/2/1 node graph and near-uniform 1I/2I/3I price ladder. A player sees one deity tree in their life. Nine talents in a fixed shape reads as 'a tree', not as 'the tenth copy of a template'. Nobody at a table has ever compared ten deity DAGs.

Cosine similarity between trees. Black↔Red 0.920, Blue↔Red 0.869, Envoy↔Scholar 0.826. No player has ever experienced a cosine. The felt version of this question is 'does my turn look like his turn', and on that measure Black (vital damage, isolation, HP costs) and Red (energy AoE, charging, Fast turns) look nothing alike — the pair the metric ranks #1 of 210.

The 39-41 shared-stock slots. A player sees the talents in their own tree. Two players in Hunter and Warrior would have to lay sheets side by side to notice Combat Training, Hardy, Mighty, Surefooted and Swift Strikes are verbatim identical, and even then the reaction is 'we're both fighters' rather than 'the design leaked'. The felt cost is only the opportunity cost of one slot, and only for a player who reads the whole tree before choosing.

Heroic damage formulas being flat across Tiers 1 and 2. `(2 + max(@tier - 2, 0))d8` first changes at Tier 3, i.e. level 11 — outside the level window of this campaign entirely. In a level 1-10 game, this is a difference that cannot occur.

Toll-booth colours generally, in the direction of the finding. A player who bought White 3 for Sovereignty never discovers it is sizing Sovereign's Favor's temp HP, because the card says '[Tier][Die]' and names no colour. But that cuts both ways and the invisible half is the harmful one: a player choosing between a third rank of Black and a third of White is choosing blind. The fix is one word on a card, not a rebalance.

Blue's five disadvantage talents 'collapsing into one'. This is only felt in the narrow case where a player owns both Pattern Recognition and False Premise and targets the same creature in the same round — both write 'their next test'. In every other configuration the five fire on different targets at different times and are five distinct effects. The primer's rule is about a second source on the SAME roll.

Interposing Shield using `half [Die]` where its two siblings Devoted Conduit and Shield Wall use `half [Tier][Die]`. At Tier 2 the costed Reaction mitigates ~2.0 and the free Passives mitigate ~4.5. A player will feel their Reaction being underwhelming; they will never diagnose it as a missing token. Almost certainly an authoring slip and a one-word fix.

Blue's Counterspell Cost field misspelling 'Investiure', which is why the deterministic census counts Blue at 15 Investiture-costers instead of 16. Invisible at the table, trivially fixable in data/leyline.json, and worth fixing only because it silently corrupts every future census run.

[MOST FELT OF THE INVISIBLE SET] Sovereignty's ±1 damage-die step. One step is worth +1.0 average per die: +2 on a two-die weapon, and against the four flat-damage riders in the game it is worth exactly zero. This is the smallest unit of effect in the corpus. It is on this list rather than in concessions only because what a player actually feels is not 'that was 1.0 points' but 'I spent my Action and my Investiture and nothing visible happened' — which makes it a PERCEPTIBILITY failure, and perceptibility failures are fixable by printing the number on the card or by moving the payload onto Sovereign's Favor's temp HP, which is unmediated and visible. That is a smaller change than the redesign three analyses propose.
fixRisks: GIVING BLUE DAMAGE. Blue↔Red already sits at 0.869 and Blue↔Black at 0.844 on the similarity matrix this review exists to reduce; adding damage raises both. It breaks Revision Principle 7 ('Talents must not bleed across color lines. … Blue manipulates probability; Red escalates momentum') and Principle 9 (human-scale). And it deletes the only sentence in Blue's player-facing description that distinguishes it — 'They rarely meet force with force.' You would be curing an overlap complaint by manufacturing overlap.

GIVING WHITE DAMAGE. White's only on-identity damage concept — punishing someone who breaks a binding term — is already implemented as deity/Order's Edict line, and Order's gate colour is White. Building it in White hollows out the deity tree sitting directly above it, which is the exact hollowing-out mechanism the White analysis identified in the other direction (Order's Shoulder the Oath already outclassing White's Shared Burden). Two trees would then compete for one idea.

BUILDING SOVEREIGNTY THE PROMISED DECREE ZONE. The corpus's single worst confirmed duplication is Civilization's Lay Foundation ≡ Fate's Ordained Ground — same Free Action, same 1 Investiture, same designate-a-square-for-the-scene, same +1 to all defenses, same sustain-up-to-tier — and both trace to the design guide handing two trees the same White brief. Adding a third ally-buff/enemy-debuff square would make it a triple. If Decree is built, it must be built on a mechanic the other two do not have (a MOVING radius centred on the arbiter, or a zone that steps dice rather than granting flat defence), or the fix creates the review's worst existing problem a third time.

MAKING SOVEREIGNTY'S DIE STEPS BIGGER. The d4-d12 clamp is not decoration. On a rank-3 ally rolling [Tier][Die] = d8, there are exactly two rungs of headroom, and Investiture of Authority (+1) and the capstone (+2) already compete for the same two — they cannot both pay out. A bigger step silently does nothing on any ally already near d10, so the buff would become MORE erratic, not less. If Sovereignty's payload is raised, raise the unmediated half (Sovereign's Favor's temp HP, Edict of the Fallen's party temp HP), which no clamp touches.

CONVERTING THE ADVANTAGE GRANTS TO STACKING `formula` MODIFIERS. The primitive exists (`edha-next-test-mod` with a summing `formula` field) but is used by exactly ONE adversary ability and by zero talents, so it is unproven at 365 scale and its only precedent is outside the scope fence. Worse, the synergy analysis independently identifies uncapped additive numeric bonuses as the ecosystem's largest balance risk — nine trees' worth of +Rank, +Tier, +command die, +White modifier landing on one roll with no cap. Converting ~15 binary grants into summing numeric ones trades a 'does nothing' problem for a 'does too much, unboundedly' problem, and pours the new modifiers into exactly the channel already flagged as uncapped.

UN-FLATTENING HEROIC DAMAGE BY ADDING A TIER MULTIPLIER. Heroic damage talents are riders on a weapon attack whose base damage already grows with equipment; leyline damage talents are self-contained and grow only through [Tier][Die]. Giving heroic riders a tier multiplier double-dips a growth channel leyline casters do not have, and would overshoot the parity target rather than reach it. The safer lever, if one is wanted, is the rank-3 gates: dropping Athletics 3+ off Devastating Blow moves heroic damage from L6 to L2 without touching a die.

'FIXING' THE EARLIEST-LEVEL CALCULATOR. It is not broken (measurementArtefacts #1). Editing a correct fixpoint calculator on the strength of six concurring analyses is the highest-probability way to introduce the bug they all described.

LIFTING THE SHARED-STOCK LAYER OUT INTO PATH-AGNOSTIC GENERAL TALENTS. Combat Training and Hardy are load-bearing managed prerequisites: Combat Training gates Devastating Blow, and Hardy gates Swift Strikes in Warrior and Unrelenting Salvo in Hunter. Removing them from the trees severs `connections` edges and is squarely iron-rule-7 territory (the review has already found two live prose-vs-connections divergences in deity/Death). The 'returns ~29 slots' figure prices the gain and not the graph repair.

ADDING SPECIALS TO THE DEITY TREES TO HIT THE 15-20% TARGET. The primer states a Special 'is worth materially more than an Action of the same effect size'. Converting deity Actions to Specials makes deity trees strictly more action-efficient, widening exactly the deity-vs-leyline gap the primer flags as the thing to watch ('9 deity talents outclassing 25 leyline talents in TOTAL would be' a bug). If deity Specials are added, leyline needs the compensating look first.

REWRITING MOMENTUM'S EDGE'S NUMBER RATHER THAN ITS TOKEN. Two analyses conclude 'the number itself has to change'. The card is arguably already correct — 'equal to your Speed' reads as the skill modifier, matching every other rider in the corpus — and the authored handler's `@movement.walk.rate` is the outlier. Redesigning the talent to fix a bad token discards a working card. Read the token first.
concessions: SOVEREIGNTY'S DECREE IS PROMISED IN THE PLAYER-FACING TEXT AND DOES NOT EXIST. INTENT-deity-Sovereignty.md prints it as a bolded '**Signature resource:** _Decree_ — a declared law projected within a radius: allies inside are elevated, enemies inside are diminished', and the deity guide repeats it under a section carrying NO 'reference, not law' disclaimer. I read all nine talents: every one targets 'a creature in Attunement Range' or 'a willing ally'; there is no zone, radius or aura anywhere. This is the one drift a player meets before they ever roll a die, because the path description is what they read when choosing a god. It is the most actionable finding in the entire review and I will not defend it. Power's Bounty is the same failure one degree softer — Warlord's Fury implements an unnamed equivalent, so it is a naming gap rather than an absence.

BLACK VIOLATES THE LEYLINE GUIDE'S ACTION-TYPE RULES OUTRIGHT: 60% Passive against Revision Principle 4's explicit 'Eliminate Passives above 35%', and 4% Special against a 25-30% target and the guide's own 'Specials are the most important gap'. The other four leyline trees complied with the same revision pass. Black did not, and no reading of the guide excuses it.

THE DEITY ATLAS HAS ZERO SPECIAL TALENTS IN 90, AGAINST A WRITTEN 15-20% TARGET. Ten trees, zero exceptions. This is a documented target missed completely, and it is the same instruction the leyline atlas successfully executed — so the standard is achievable and was simply not applied to deity.

ADVANTAGE IS BINARY AND SOME TALENTS ARE WRITTEN AS IF IT IS NOT. Hunter's Fatal Thrust ('gain two advantages if the weapon is Discreet') and Warrior's Defensive Position ('adds two disadvantages… instead of one') describe a stacking model the engine cannot represent. Both are unwired (hasEvents=false), so this is a card-text ruling rather than an engine defect — but a player who reads 'two advantages' and receives one has been told something false by their own sheet. That is felt immediately and it should be fixed by wording, not left standing.

THE ENGINE HAS TWO TEMPORARY-HP WRITERS WITH OPPOSITE BEHAVIOUR. `edhaGrantTempHpCross` keeps the higher; `edhaWriteTempHp` replaces unconditionally, with its own header saying a new grant 'OVERWRITES the old, even if smaller'. On the overwriting routes — the generic single-target path, Life's heal-overflow grants, the total-dealt grant — a smaller grant deletes a larger pool. Fourteen talents produce temp HP. This is a live bug with a felt consequence (a player's shield gets smaller when an ally helps them), and no card text can be written until the writers are unified.

TWO IRON-RULE-7 PROSE/CONNECTIONS DIVERGENCES ARE LIVE ON MAIN, BOTH IN deity/Death. Raise Dead's card says 'Necrotic Cascade or Speak with the Fallen' while its connections array is ['Necrotic Cascade','Risen Servant']; Necrotic Cascade's card says 'Consuming Decay' while its connections are ['Consuming Decay','Death Ward']. Connections are managed prerequisites, so in both cases Foundry demands a talent the card does not, and the player is simply blocked. This is the sharpest kind of felt defect and it is cheap to fix.

MOMENTUM'S EDGE IS BROKEN ONE WAY OR THE OTHER. Its authored handler reads `@movement.walk.rate`. If that resolves, the talent is a free depth-2 Passive delivering ~+20-30 flat impact against 1-4 for every other rider in the game; if it does not resolve, the talent silently delivers nothing. Neither is acceptable and both are live now. My only qualification is about which end to fix (see fixRisks), not about whether.

KNOWLEDGE'S DAMAGE CEILING IS AN OUTLIER AND THE CENSUS CANNOT SEE IT. The per-Insight multiplication lives in an authored `edha-damage-bonus` amountFormula — `((@tier)d(2 * @colorRank + 2)) * max(@counter, 1)` — not in `damage.formula`, so every future census that ranks damage from `damageFormula` will place the highest-ceiling tree in the game near the bottom. Whether the ceiling is ever realised depends on a single target surviving three rounds, which is an adversary-durability question the scope fence excludes; but the measurement blindness is repo-side and real.

WHITE AND BLUE HAVE AN AGENCY PROBLEM THAT IS NOT A DAMAGE PROBLEM, AND IT IS REAL. White has one 1-Action and one 2-Action talent in 25; Blue's Action-costing kit is thin and its three teeth (Counterspell, Ghostly Walls into Absolute Stillness, Anticipate) are all L6. My defence — that White converts Draw Mana into a party heal plus a condition strip, that seven Reactions with five trigger classes mean a rarely-idle slot, that Blue's Probable Outcome rewrites turn order free and forever — softens this. It does not dissolve it. A player wants their own turn to be the moment their sheet matters, and both trees ask them to wait for someone else's. The designer's instinct that something needs re-evaluating is correct; his proposed remedy (damage) is the wrong one.

THREE OF WHITE'S SEVEN REACTIONS GENUINELY COLLIDE. Interposing Shield ('an ally within 10 feet takes damage'), Retributive Guard ('an ally adjacent to you takes damage from an enemy') and Shared Burden ('an ally adjacent to you takes damage') all fire on the same event into the same one slot. A player holding all three has bought two talents that will almost never fire. This is a smaller and truer finding than 'seven Reactions compete for one slot', and unlike that one it is worth acting on.
caseForBlueWhiteSovereigntyAsIs:
BLUE — the strongest case of the three, and I largely believe it. Blue's binding intent source promises three specialties and delivers all three: Foresight (Forewarned, Intercept, Reactive Analysis, Telepathic Network, Probable Outcome, Read Intent, Anticipate), Calculation (Pattern Recognition, Counterspell, False Premise, Subtle Suggestion, Baleful, Probability Cascade), Illusion (eight talents, and a grep of all 365 shows Blue is the only tree in the game that CREATES illusions — Green's Natural Order and Chaos's Unweaving merely see through or strip them). Blue owns three things nothing else in the corpus has: Counterspell, the only effect that makes another character's talent FAIL as it is activated; the illusion subsystem; and Probable Outcome — "After all creatures choose fast or slow turn, you may change your choice" — which is the only talent in 365 that rewrites turn order after declaration, is free, permanent, untriggered, and available at L3. In a system where Fast turns resolve before Slow turns, being the only character at the table who chooses last is a tempo and information edge in every round of every fight forever. Not one of the thirteen analyses priced it; Blue's own verified profile does not list it in its top three. Add Telepathic Network (scene-long party telepathy that shares your expertise), Living Image (a moving, conversing illusion), and Read Intent (the GM tells you an enemy's next action), and Blue is the best out-of-combat problem-solver in the leyline atlas — an axis the combat-weighted rubric scores at 3. The plot-die complaint, which five analyses call Blue's real defect, cites a design-guide line inside a section headed "reference, not law". VERDICT: I believe this. Blue's problem is not identity or emptiness; it is that its three best cards are L6 and its early game is thin. That is a pacing fix (move one tooth to depth 1), not an identity fix, and certainly not damage.

WHITE — a good case that I believe about 70%. White is the only colour whose refuel Action is itself an effect: the Key heals every ally in range for Tier on every Draw Mana, and Beacon of Stability is a Special that rides that same Draw Mana to strip a condition. So White's "wasted" 50%-uptime Action is a party heal plus a condition removal — the one tree in the game with no dead round, which exactly inverts the "White's turn is empty" reading. Its free, permanent, untriggered, multi-target mitigation (Guardian Stance from L1, Devoted Conduit, Shield Wall) is the best-in-class implementation of the thing its path description promises: "Where they stand, lines hold." Its seven Reactions have five distinct trigger classes, so its single slot is rarely idle — coverage, not redundancy. And its action-light shape is Revision Principle 1 ("Specials first") plus the primer's "a talent that reproduces a standard action is worth roughly zero" carried to their conclusion. VERDICT: I believe the mitigation half and the Draw Mana half completely. I do not believe the agency half. Three of the seven Reactions fire on the same event, White's own damage source is a single contested Reaction, and a player will still spend rounds watching. The right change is one repeatable, self-initiated, on-your-turn play at low depth — not a damage talent.

SOVEREIGNTY — the weakest of the three, and I only half believe it. What survives honest reading: it is not empty. Sovereign's Favor grants [Tier][Die] temporary HP on every Exalt (~3.5 at Tier 1, ~9.0 at Tier 2), unmediated by the die ladder, repeatable every round from L2. Expose is a free L2 Passive that generates Investiture uncapped and converts every enemy miss into an ally Reactive Strike. Edict of the Fallen is a scene-long −2 die steps on an enemy's attacks against EVERYONE at any range in Attunement Range, plus party temp HP on every miss, for 2 Actions once at L3 — larger than the "weakest debuff" one analysis compared to White's best mitigation. The capstone's third clause, which the analysis ranking Sovereignty last never quotes, is a scene-long enemy reaction lock triggered whenever the exalted ally hits — and the primer says action denial is the most valuable category in a 3-action economy. Its die-size monopoly is genuine (7 of 7 hits in 365). And the "nine axes at zero" headline is a 9-vs-25 talent-count artefact, while "damage_direct 0" is the rubric having no cell for an amplifier that never swings. VERDICT: I do not fully believe it. Two things defeat the defence, and neither is arithmetic. First, the promised Decree is in the player-facing text and in no talent — the player is mis-sold before the campaign starts. Second, the tree's headline lever moves an enemy's damage roll by about one point per die, which is below the threshold at which a human at a table perceives that anything happened. A tree can be mathematically paid for and still fail, and this one fails on perceptibility. But the remedy is smaller than the review implies: print the payload where it can be seen (move value onto Sovereign's Favor and Edict of the Fallen, both unmediated), name the governing colour on the cards, and build Decree as something the other two zone talents are not.
